meta.name: The Prince of Tennis II U-17 WORLD CUP
meta.description: The story follows the unfolding of the U-17 World Cup, which takes place at the KCC Arena, in Melbourne, Australia. A total of 32 countries are participating in this long-awaited competition, and only 16 of them will manage to qualify for the final stages…

videos.title: Team USA, Ryoma Echizen
videos.overview: After Ryoma is forced to withdraw from the Japan U-17 training camp, Ryoga invites him to play for the US team.

videos.title: Pre-World Cup Kicks Off!
videos.overview: Teams from all over the world competing in the U-17 World Cup gather to start things off with the Pre-World Cup exhibition matches.

videos.title: A Moment Ahead in the Future
videos.overview: Pre-World Cup (World Cup), 3rd match. In the champion Germany, captain Bork finally goes to the court. The challenge is the Tokugawa & Yukimura pair. However, shortly after the start of the game, Yukimura was "deprived of his five senses." Tokugawa will fight alone against the German pair while hiding Yukimura. Meanwhile, Yukimura was also fighting loneliness. Yukimura's ears, deprived of his five senses and fighting "fear alone" in the closed darkness, heard his voice overcoming it while being deprived of his five senses.

videos.title: Prince vs Prince
videos.overview: Japan's Pre-World Cup match ended. After seeing the match and leaving the venue, Ryoma encounters Sakurano, who is entwined by local bad guys. Doberman attacks Ryoma, who confronts the bad guys while sheltering Sakurano. It was a boy who straddled Hakuba who rejected it. He shoots the ball with a tennis racket while straddling a horse and drives away the bad guys. Ryoma, who was mistaken for a boyfriend by a boy who was fascinated by Sakurano, was challenged to play a game, and they would fight each other in tennis while riding horses.

videos.title: Upset
videos.overview: Finally, the World Cup main draw will begin. Japan's first opponent is the Greek national team. If they manage to beat them, their next round opponent would be the Australia who has managed to beat, Switzerland, who was ranked 2nd in the world.

videos.title: Absolute Away Game
videos.overview: In the Japan team's first doubles match against Australia, Sanada's tricky shots initially baffle his opponents, but they quickly adapt their defense.

videos.title: Chess King
videos.overview: The Japan team plays with renewed vigor following Atobe’s cunning ruse. Finally figuring out Milman’s Tachyon serve, Fuji moves to break the deadlock.

videos.title: One's Resolve... One's Conditions
videos.overview: Discouraged by two straight doubles losses, the Japan team heads into the singles matches. Akutsu goes up against the menacing Swiss captain, Amadeus.

videos.title: Feelings for My Friends
videos.overview: After seeing Akutsu's match against Switzerland, Ryoma seems to have developed some feelings of doubt within him...

videos.title: Beyond the Bible
videos.overview: Ryoma finally returns to the Japan national team. With Ryoma as a member, the opponent in the quarterfinals will be France, ranked 3rd in the world. Shiraishi, who was selected as a member, was worried about whether his "honor student" tennis would be able to compete against the world.

videos.title: The Worst Doubles Pair
videos.overview: After Yanagi rebukes Mori for his past attitude toward training, the two must overcome their differences if they want to beat their French opponents.

videos.title: Prince of Ace
videos.overview: Ryoma's match with Chardard continues in three singles matches of Japan versus France; the victorious team will advance to play Germany.

videos.title: Samurai vs Knight
videos.overview: Ryoma's match with Chardard continues.

videos.title: The Mightiest Germany: The Night Before the Match!
videos.overview: The Japanese team is resolutely preparing for the match against Germany, aiming to advance to the finals afterward. Captain Byodoin trusts his players, who do not give up despite this challenge.

videos.title: Bluebird
videos.overview: In the first match of the U-17 World Cup Semifinals it's Team Japan's Oni versus Team Germany's Q･P. Can Oni hold his ground against Team Germany's No. 2 player?

videos.title: For Whom Do You Grow Strong
videos.overview: The first match of the World Cup Semifinals continues between Oni and Q･P. Oni shines with a mysterious light that resembles the Pinnacle of Perfection and becomes seemingly invincible.

videos.title: The Final Illusion
videos.overview: In the next match, Team Japan's Duke and Nio face off against Schneider and Belti, two of the three tennis pros on Team Germany.

videos.title: Tezuka vs. Yukimura
videos.overview: Continuing the World Cup Semifinals is Team Germany’s Tezuka versus Team Japan’s Yukimura in #2 singles. Tezuka is now their opponent, so Team Japan goes all out to gain victory against their former teammate.

videos.title: Zero Senses Tennis
videos.overview: Yukimura prepares to counter Tezuka's Pinnacle of Perfection in order to prove to Akaya, his team, and himself that you don't have to give up on tennis even if you can't use the Pinnacle of Perfection.

videos.title: The Future Beyond the Fierce Match
videos.overview: Every time Yukimura takes away Tezuka's five senses, Tezuka regaains them using the Pinnacle of Perfection. Can Yukimura be able to turn the tables or will Tezuka hold on to his lead?

videos.title: Team Spain, Ryoga Echizen
videos.overview: In the other semifinals bracket, Team USA is competing with Team Spain for a spot at the finals. Ryoga Echizen, who is now playing for Team Spain, clashes with Ralph Reinhart of Team USA.

videos.title: Focus Burst vs. Pinnacle of Perfection
videos.overview: Kirihara is determined to beat Siegfried's Pinnacle of Perfection with his Focus Burst. The two battle it out as their doubles partners watch on.

videos.title: The Outcome of the Tiebreak
videos.overview: The second set of the doubles match between Tanegashima-Kirihara and Bismarck-Siegfried gets drawn into a tiebreak. If Team Japan loses this set, they will be eliminated from the semifinals.

videos.title: Final Set
videos.overview: The doubles pairs Tanegashima-Kirihara and Bismarck-Siegfried ramp it up for this final set, showing teamwork that activates skills never seen before.

videos.title: Spiral Baptism
videos.overview: In the last match of the semifinals, Byodoin and Volk go head-to-head in a mighty battle to bring their teams through to the finals.

videos.title: Life-or-Death Tennis
videos.overview: Byodoin puts his life on the line against Germany's Volk in an intense epilogue to the World Cup semifinals.

videos.title: Team Japan's Next Challenge
videos.overview: Team Japan will soon face Spain in the final match, but who will compete? There's only one way to decide.

videos.title: The Selection Match Begins!
videos.overview: Nostalgic pairs and repeated rivals, each player battles to secure their spot on the Team. Even...

videos.title: Men Who Never Give Up
videos.overview: Heated battles on every court, Sanada and Marui strive to improve their skills while giving it their all!

videos.title: The Moon and the Sun
videos.overview: Atobe and Oshitari clash rackets as they reflect on the past and speak their mind through tennis.

videos.title: A Decision Named Doubles
videos.overview: Nioh, Mori, and Kintaro's potentials are tested for this second match as their seniors push their limits.

videos.title: If Ya Get Hit, Hit 'em Back!
videos.overview: Diving into Kintaro's past, the winners of the last doubles match for this 2nd tournament round to be decided!

videos.title: The Masked Man
videos.overview: Days before the final, Momo was attacked by someone, but who? Spain's mysterious players come to light.

videos.title: Solely Aim for Victory
videos.overview: With the third matches starting, everyone is putting their all on the line with only victory in mind!
